questions.question: A number line starts at 5 and ends at 6. It is divided into 10 equal parts, so each small step is 0.1. Nadia wants to mark √30 on this line. Which statement is correct?
options: √30 goes 5 steps past 5, because 30 is between 25 and 36
√30 does not belong here; it is between √16 = 4 and √25 = 5
√30 does not belong here, since 30 ÷ 2 = 15 is far past 6
√30 belongs 5 steps past 5 and equals exactly 5.5 there
questions.explain: Use the neighbouring perfect squares: √25 = 5 and √36 = 6, and 30 is a bit closer to 25, so √30 ≈ 5.5 — five 0.1-steps past 5. A square root is not the number halved, and 5.5 is only an estimate (5.5 × 5.5 = 30.25).

questions.question: A number line runs from 6 to 7 and is cut into 10 equal parts, so each part is worth 0.1. Where should √44 be marked on this line?
options: The line is wrong, because √44 sits between √49 = 7 and √64 = 8
6 steps past 6, because 44 is nearer 49 than 36: √44 ≈ 6.6
The line is wrong, because √44 means 44 ÷ 2 = 22, far past 7
6 steps past 6, because √44 is exactly equal to 6.6 there
questions.explain: 36 and 49 are the perfect squares on either side of 44, so √44 is between 6 and 7; 44 is closer to 49, so √44 ≈ 6.6. Watch out: 6.6 × 6.6 = 43.56, so 6.6 is an estimate, not the exact value.

questions.question: A number line goes from 7 to 8 and is split into 10 equal parts, each worth 0.1. Kim marks √55 at the point 4 steps past 7. Is Kim right?
options: Yes, and that point shows √55 is exactly equal to 7.4
No, because √55 lies between √36 = 6 and √49 = 7 instead
Yes, because 55 is nearer 49 than 64, so √55 ≈ 7.4
No, because √55 means 55 ÷ 2 = 27.5, far past this line
questions.explain: 49 and 64 are the perfect squares around 55, and 55 is nearer 49, so √55 ≈ 7.4 — four 0.1-steps past 7. The pair must sit on either side of 55, and 7.4 × 7.4 = 54.76 shows this is an estimate.

questions.question: A number line stretches from 3 to 4 and is divided into 10 equal parts, so one part is 0.1. Where does √14 belong?
options: This line will not work: √14 sits between √16 = 4 and √25 = 5
This line will not work: √14 means 14 ÷ 2 = 7, far past 4
At 7 parts past 3, and that makes √14 exactly equal to 3.7
At 7 parts past 3, since 14 is nearer 16 than 9: ≈ 3.7
questions.explain: 9 and 16 are the perfect squares on either side of 14, and 14 is much nearer 16, so √14 ≈ 3.7. Check the pair surrounds your number, and remember 3.7 × 3.7 = 13.69, so it is close but not exact.

questions.question: Estimate √83 to one decimal place. Which answer, with its reason, is best?
options: 9.1, because 83 is just past the square 81 = 9²
41.5, because a square root means half of 83
8.1, because 83 lies between the squares 64 and 81
9.1 exactly, because 9.1 × 9.1 comes to exactly 83
questions.explain: 83 sits between 81 = 9² and 100 = 10², and it is only 2 above 81, so √83 ≈ 9.1. Since 9.1 × 9.1 = 82.81, say 'about 9.1' rather than 'equals 9.1'.

questions.question: A square vegetable plot at a Surrey community garden covers 40 m². About how long is one side, to one decimal place?
options: About 5.7 m, since 40 lies between 25 and 36
About 6.3 m, since 40 is just above 36 = 6²
About 20 m, since a square root is half of 40
Exactly 6.3 m, since 6.3 × 6.3 gives 40 m²
questions.explain: The side is √40; the perfect squares around 40 are 36 and 49, and 40 is close to 36, so the side ≈ 6.3 m. Note 6.3 × 6.3 = 39.69, so this length is an estimate, not exact.

questions.question: Kai estimates √52 ≈ 7.2 for a math journal entry. Is 7.2 exactly equal to √52?
options: Yes, √52 is equal to 7.2 once you round it
No, √52 is between 6 and 7, so 7.2 is too big
No, 7.2 × 7.2 = 51.84, so √52 is a bit more
No, √52 means 52 ÷ 2 = 26, so 7.2 is too small
questions.explain: 52 sits between 49 = 7² and 64 = 8² and is near 49, so √52 ≈ 7.2 — but squaring 7.2 gives 51.84, just under 52, so the true root is slightly larger. An estimate uses ≈, never =.

questions.question: Estimate √8 to one decimal place, using the perfect squares beside 8.
options: 3.2, because 8 lies between the squares 9 and 16
2.8, because 2.8 × 2.8 is exactly equal to 8
4.0, because the square root of 8 is 8 ÷ 2
2.8, because 8 is quite close to the square 9
questions.explain: 4 = 2² and 9 = 3² surround 8, and 8 is much nearer 9, so √8 ≈ 2.8. The neighbours must be on both sides of 8, and 2.8 × 2.8 = 7.84 shows 2.8 is an estimate.

questions.question: A square patio in Kelowna will cover 90 m². The family wants metal edging along all four sides at $12 per metre. About how much will the edging cost?
options: About $456, from a side of about 9.5 m (81 and 100)
About $408, using a side of 8.5 m from 64 and 81
About $2160, using a side of 45 m, since 90 ÷ 2 = 45
Exactly $456, since the side is exactly 9.5 m long
questions.explain: First estimate the side: 90 lies between 81 = 9² and 100 = 10², closer to 81, so √90 ≈ 9.5 m; then 4 × 9.5 = 38 m and 38 × $12 = about $456. Because 9.5 is an estimate, the cost is approximate too.

questions.question: Devon writes: '√72 ≈ 7.5, because 72 lies between 49 and 64.' What is the mistake?
options: The pair should be 81 and 100, so √72 ≈ 9.1
72 is past 64, so use 64 and 81: √72 ≈ 8.5
The step missed is halving: √72 is 72 ÷ 2 = 36
Nothing is wrong, since √72 is exactly 7.5
questions.explain: The two perfect squares must sit on either side of 72: 64 = 8² and 81 = 9², and 72 is a little nearer 64, so √72 ≈ 8.5. Always check your pair actually traps the number before estimating the decimal.

questions.question: Ravi has a square garden bed of 45 m² and Maya has a square bed of 60 m². About how much longer is Maya's side than Ravi's?
options: About 7.5 m, since the sides are 30 m and 22.5 m
About 2.0 m, since the sides are 8.7 m and 6.7 m
About 1.0 m, since the sides are 7.7 m and 6.7 m
Exactly 1.0 m, since the sides are 7.7 m and 6.7 m
questions.explain: Estimate each side first: 45 is between 36 and 49 (nearer 49) so √45 ≈ 6.7, and 60 is between 49 and 64 (nearer 64) so √60 ≈ 7.7; the difference is about 1.0 m. Both sides are estimates, so the difference is 'about', not exact.

questions.question: On a worksheet Jayden writes √23 = 4.8. Ella says the sign should be ≈ instead of =. Who is right, and why?
options: Jayden — 4.8 is the rounded value, so it equals √23
Ella — √23 is between √25 = 5 and √36 = 6, so 4.8 is low
Ella — √23 means 23 ÷ 2 = 11.5, so 4.8 is far too low
questions.explain: 16 and 25 surround 23, and 23 is near 25, so √23 ≈ 4.8 — but 4.8 squared is 23.04, so 4.8 only comes close. An estimate from neighbouring perfect squares always gets ≈, never =.
